Never fetched by the student's browser until a teacher/marker PDF is generated (formative: automatically when the student clicks Generate; assessed: only via the ?teacher=1-gated action, after Final Submit). Never render any of this on the student-facing page. See CLAUDE.md §5's assessment-security amendment.

markingScheme.criterion: Identifies a real trend from their own logged years (e.g. the level fell fastest in years with high extraction and a drought event; or a conservation measure clearly slowed the decline once switched on) AND gives the correct cause-and-effect mechanism linking rainfall, extraction and recharge to the change in reservoir level (extraction and evaporation remove water; rainfall and recharge add it back; the balance of the two sets the level).
markingScheme.accept: Any genuine trend quoting at least one of their own logged years' rainfall/extraction/recharge/level values, paired with an equivalent mechanism explanation.
markingScheme.insufficient: Stating 'the level went down' with no actual figures quoted from their own record, or a mechanism given with no year/reading referenced.

markingScheme.criterion: States clearly whether the evidence supported or contradicted their own recorded hypothesis, with a stated confidence level.
markingScheme.accept: Any judgement (supported/not supported/partially supported) consistent with their own data, with any stated confidence level (e.g. 'fairly confident', 'not very confident').
markingScheme.insufficient: Repeating the hypothesis wording without saying whether the evidence agreed with it, or giving no confidence level at all.

markingScheme.criterion: Names something that would make the investigation more reliable (e.g. repeating the run with the same strategy to see if the random rainfall pattern changes the outcome, or testing the opposite strategy for comparison).
markingScheme.accept: Any genuine reliability improvement — repeating the run, changing one variable at a time, comparing against an opposite strategy, or averaging multiple runs.
markingScheme.insufficient: A vague statement like 'be more careful' with no concrete way to actually improve the investigation's reliability.

markingScheme.criterion: Gives a sensible extraction change (e.g. capping agricultural extraction, since agriculture uses the largest share of water) with a reason linked to what raised or lowered the level in the simulation.
markingScheme.accept: Any specific extraction change (agricultural, industrial or domestic) linked to a correct reason grounded in the simulation.
markingScheme.insufficient: A vague 'use less water' with no specific extraction category or link to the simulation.

markingScheme.criterion: Gives a SECOND, genuinely distinct suggestion: a sensible conservation measure (drip irrigation, rainwater harvesting or wetland restoration) with a correct explanation of how it changes recharge or reduces demand — not a restatement of the first point.
markingScheme.accept: Any one of the three conservation measures modelled in the simulation, correctly explained; recognising that rainfall itself cannot be controlled directly, and that management therefore has to work through extraction and recharge instead, is also acceptable content here.
markingScheme.insufficient: Repeating the extraction change from the first point in different words, rather than a genuinely different lever.

markingScheme.criterion: Acknowledges a genuine trade-off (e.g. cutting agricultural extraction may reduce farm income, so a real city has to balance water security against other needs).
markingScheme.accept: Any realistic cost or downside attached to the suggested changes, showing the student understands management is a balance, not a free win.
markingScheme.insufficient: Claiming the suggested changes have no downside or cost at all.

= the Explain question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one (trend + mechanism, hypothesis judgement, reliability improvement). Do not award these 3 marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: No real trend identified from own data, or no mechanism given linking rainfall, extraction and recharge to the reservoir level.
Identifies a real trend from own data with a plausible mechanism, but does not compare it against the recorded hypothesis or state a confidence level.
Identifies a trend with a correct mechanism AND compares it against the recorded hypothesis with a confidence level, but does not name anything that would make the investigation more reliable.

Identifies a real trend from own data with a correct cause-and-effect mechanism, states whether it supported or contradicted the recorded hypothesis with a confidence level, and names something that would make the investigation more reliable.

criteria.source: = the Apply question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one (extraction change, conservation measure, trade-off). Do not award these 3 marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: No credible management suggestions, or suggestions are not based on anything observed in the simulation.
Gives one sensible management change grounded in the simulation, but the second suggestion or the trade-off is missing or unconvincing.
Gives two sensible management changes grounded in the simulation with correct reasoning, but does not acknowledge a genuine trade-off.
Gives two sensible management changes grounded in the simulation with correct reasoning for each, and acknowledges a genuine real-world trade-off.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across BOTH the Explain and Apply answers together — independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks in use_of_evidence and reasoning above.

levels.descriptor: Hard to follow, or environmental-science terms are missing or incorrect.
Understandable, but with unclear phrasing or a misused term.
Clear, full sentences using correct environmental-science terminology (e.g. extraction, recharge, evaporation, scarcity).

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply). Award marks point-by-point using each question's marking_scheme in marking_context: each point is worth the marks stated, is independent unless it names a dependsOn point (in which case only award it if that earlier point was also awarded), and each point's 'accept'/'insufficient' tell you exactly what does and doesn't count. use_of_evidence's 3 marks ARE the Explain marking_scheme's 3 points, and reasoning's 3 marks ARE the Apply marking_scheme's 3 points — the rubric levels restate the same points as bands; award each set of 3 marks ONCE, not twice. communication is a separate, holistic 2 marks across both answers' clarity and vocabulary, never overlapping with the content marks. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy (5 marks = full). Use the student's actual logged years (the rainfall/extraction/recharge/level/interventions columns in simulation_results.trials) to verify any reading or year the student claims to quote — do not take their prose summary on trust if it does not match their own logged data. Accept scientifically valid alternative wording per each point's 'accept' field, and do not penalise spelling unless meaning is unclear. Total is out of 13 (5 auto + 3 + 3 + 2); report the percentage, one strength, one correction and one next step, all under 80 words.
